value.body: An MA in Human Resource Management (also called MA HRM, MA in Personnel Management or MA HRM & Labour Relations) is a two-year degree on recruitment, compensation, labour law, industrial relations, training and organisational behaviour. Compared with an MBA-HR, it is narrower and more focused on HR and labour law, with fewer general-management subjects.

items.label: Usual comparison
items.note: Broader management curriculum; admissions via CAT, MAT, XAT and similar

items.label: PG students in Human Resource Management
items.note: Listed under Management; MBA-HR students are often reported under Business Administration instead. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

items.label: Students in M.H.R.D. (Master of HR Development)
items.note: One related programme title; all years, all modes. Counts only institutions that responded to AISHE, so national totals may be higher.

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A bachelor's degree in any stream. Admission is through university entrance tests, CUET-PG at participating universities, or graduation marks, sometimes followed by an interview.

value.title: At a glance
items: Recruiters often treat MBA-HR and MA HRM graduates differently, so check the placement record of the specific programme.
Labour law and industrial relations knowledge suits manufacturing and public-sector HR roles.
Common entry roles: HR executive, recruiter, payroll and compliance.
